analysis: Both options have a substantial spine of historical periods and themes, historical research, material evidence, historiography and visual culture. The closest option broadens the historical and source base through Greek archaeology, empires, literary accounts, art histories and historical political cases. The required History Research Seminar supports source criticism and independent written argument.

The public-memory option retains the historical spine and deliberately adds representation, oral and community inquiry, museum interpretation, documentary production and audience-facing rhetoric. Native American Histories and Media & Race provide direct examples of public historical interpretation, not merely communication courses. The schedule leaves UvA’s dedicated medieval history, Dutch history, digital laboratory and thesis visible as distinct requirements.

academicConstruction: Screened active GOSHIST, MCCHEAM, literature, politics and media offerings by chronology, methods and contribution to each concept. Greek Archaeology, World Archaeology and Heritage & Ancient Democracy provide real historical and material evidence for antiquity but cannot provide the medieval continuity and specialist sources needed for a separate period-led programme. Course planning is not the reason for declining that direction. In the public-memory schedule Rhetoric in Action moves from 2028h1 to 2027h1; The Documentary moves from 2027h1 to 2028h1, keeping the same course sets and placing practice after initial media and rhetoric work.
